solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Again start to take for granted after loss of pressure

indicators.note: once something is lost it is gone, so the letter for pressure is removed from the synonym

parts.note: to presume something is to take it for granted
P is the standard symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone who stopped assuming things, and then started assuming them again once the strain eased.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to begin again after a pause, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Apple Hardy heroine picked up after run finishing early

indicators.note: the reversed heroine is placed after the shortened run
the word run stops before its final letter, ending early
in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the name is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's best-known heroine

explanation.surface: A literary allusion: Hardy's heroine collecting apples after a run cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'picked up' reads the name upwards. 'Apple' looks like it qualifies the heroine but stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Russet is a variety of eating apple with a rough brownish skin, so this is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Clear ship at sea will get round

indicators.note: something at sea is confused or adrift, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Cleaning out a ship's hold before it goes on a round voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges CLEARSHIP into the answer; 'will get' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spherical is shaped like a ball, which is to say round.

clue.text: Skulk about church after feeling diminished

indicators.note: the church abbreviation comes after the shortened word
made smaller, so the synonym loses its last letter

parts.note: a mood is a feeling or state of mind

explanation.surface: Someone lurking around a church, their spirits low.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is two words: 'Skulk about' together, not 'Skulk' with 'about' as an indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is to loiter or wander aimlessly, much like skulking around.

clue.text: Heads for Tower Hamlets: spots a party

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters, so the opening letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone with a skin complaint making for a party in Tower Hamlets, a borough of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrash is informal British slang for a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Advertisement brought in these unusual phones?

indicators.note: one piece is brought into the middle of the other, so the abbreviation goes inside
out of the ordinary, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An advert promoting some unusual new phones.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'phones' is a loose definition, short for headphones.
explanation.definitionFit: Headphones are also called a headset, so phones (short for headphones) defines it.

clue.text: A quiet wood

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A peaceful spot among the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a tree whose timber is a common hardwood, so it is an example of a wood.

clue.text: Announcer arrested after intervention by artist

indicators.note: the artist intervenes, coming between the letters of the arrest word

parts.note: someone arrested is held by police
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist

explanation.surface: A broadcaster detained once a painter stepped in.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald was an official messenger who proclaimed news, so one who announces.

clue.text: Education employee having variety of chocolates given to her

indicators.note: the word her is given to the jumbled chocolates, placed after them
a variety is a mixed assortment, so the letters are shuffled together

explanation.surface: A grateful pupil handing a teacher an assorted box of chocolates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges CHOCOLATES into SCHOOLTEAC, and 'given to' adds HER at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A school teacher is employed in education, working in a school.

clue.text: All wet or sloppy around one? Things can dry here

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the single letter standing for one
something sloppy is messy and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A soaking, messy bathroom, with someone wondering where to dry things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloppy' rearranges ALLWETOR, and 'around' wraps it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel rail is a bar on which towels hang to dry.

clue.text: Planet seen in the art here

indicators.note: the answer can be seen inside the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A planet depicted in the paintings on display here.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the planet we live on, third from the Sun.

clue.text: Pensive, will shortly set about weird stuff, mostly

indicators.note: the shortened will is placed about the other letters, surrounding them
cut short, so the word will loses its final letter
strange, so these letters are put in a new order
most of the word stuff, so its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone thoughtful who will soon tackle some odd material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' gives WIL; 'mostly' gives STUF, which 'weird' rearranges to ISTFU after taking only those letters. 'set about' puts WIL round ISTFU, with ISTFU between WI and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistful means sadly thoughtful or longing, close to pensive.

clue.text: Wonderful enthusiast starts to tell company about wine

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast or devotee

indicators.note: the two initial letters go about the wine, one either side
the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A wine lover telling friends about a marvellous bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes T and C; 'about' puts them either side of ASTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic is a colloquial word for excellent or marvellous.

clue.text: Fake map including US city and area north

indicators.note: the city abbreviation is included within the map word

parts.note: a chart is a map, especially for navigation
LA is Los Angeles
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A forged map showing an American city and the region to its north.
explanation.walkthrough: Fake here is a noun, a person who fakes things.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a fraud or impostor, someone who is a fake.

clue.text: Item in magazine showing extraction of power from proton, say

indicators.note: extraction pulls something out, so the letter for power is taken away

parts.note: a proton is an example of a subatomic particle, hence the say
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A science magazine running a feature on getting energy from protons.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a piece of writing published in a magazine or newspaper.

clue.text: Unethical having exam in the morning

indicators.note: an exam held in the morning is read with the morning abbreviation first, then the exam word

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Something shady about a candidate sitting a test before noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral means lacking moral principles, and so not ethical.

clue.text: Religious figures clear — not a good year

indicators.note: the word marks the letter that must be left out of clear

explanation.surface: Priests ruling that it has plainly been a bad twelve months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes A from CLEAR, leaving CLER.
explanation.definitionFit: The clergy are the body of priests and ministers, figures in religion.

clue.text: Armed force I illuminated entering target, but retreating

indicators.note: the letters go into the middle of the reversed target word
going backwards, so the target word is read in reverse

parts.note: an aim is a target or goal
lit means lit up or illuminated

explanation.surface: Troops lighting up a target and then falling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns AIM into MIA; 'entering' puts ILIT inside it, after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a military force raised from civilians, so an armed force.

clue.text: Weak King restricted by collapse

indicators.note: the king letter is hemmed in, held within the collapse word

parts.note: to fail is to collapse or break down
R is from Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An enfeebled monarch hemmed in by his own downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Frail means physically delicate or feeble, a synonym of weak.

clue.text: Navy supports holding line

indicators.note: the support word holds the line letter inside it

parts.note: feet are what support a person or a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A navy that keeps the battle line supplied and backed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleet is a country's navy, its whole body of warships.

clue.text: Opening given to hobbyist — a money-gathering job

parts.note: a rent is a tear or opening in fabric
a collector gathers stamps, coins and so on as a hobby

explanation.surface: Handing a hobbyist a business opening as a money-gathering post.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent here is the noun for a tear, not a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent collector's work is calling on tenants to gather the money they owe their landlord.

clue.text: Lifting barrel to find seed

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting raises the word up, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel

explanation.surface: Hoisting a barrel to look for grain inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut is a hard-shelled seed or fruit, such as a hazelnut.

clue.text: Subsequently swathing top of head in soap

indicators.note: to swathe is to wrap around, so the later word wraps round the letter

parts.note: later means subsequently, afterwards

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Wrapping up your head in shampoo suds once you are done.
explanation.definitionFit: Lather is the froth produced by soap and water, so the noun for soapy foam.

clue.text: Cane applied to boy's rear? That could be awkward

indicators.note: the stick is put against the last letter, coming first in the answer

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick or rod

indicators.note: the rear of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned corporal punishment, a boy caned on the backside, and the trouble it might bring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear' takes Y, the last letter of 'boy's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky situation is a tricky, difficult one, an informal sense of awkward.
